answer: Each identity anchors to one registered amateur telescope. Each epoch the protocol names an asteroid transit and a violet filter band; the scope must capture a fresh CCD frame of the asteroid on its predicted path, nonce-signed. A second umber-light frame checks its color against ephemeris, yarrow meadow in frame proving the site is real. One scope, one identity: shared mounts report identical frames and collapse to one vote; forged frames fail cross-checks with neighbors. A farm wanting 100 votes must buy, site, and staff 100 scopes at 100 dark sites, about $800 each plus $60 a year upkeep.
